summary: My blocker is repaired in the exact form I asked for, and the blocker I missed is repaired under the rule that governs it. C2-SAT-B1: the proposed lead now retires both occurrences of the 'nets to zero SATISFIED rows' sentence and the 'LIVE standing is OPEN' clause to history, and supplies the accounting I asked for -- DR-001 becomes the first SATISFIED row of the eleven, condition 1 still does not discharge. CX-DR001-D044-B1, which Codex found and I did not, is real: blueprint §1.1's CLAIMS row pins claim-register.v1.json at 95097b3f… while live bytes and baseline /sources/3 are both 767dc210…. I read blueprint reading rule 1 verbatim -- 'If a file's digest differs from the value below, stop and record a design delta; do not build the bytes you found' -- and R6 is precisely that disposition, quoted accurately, with the live binding named authoritatively. I re-ran every measurement this turn rather than accepting 'unchanged': 49/49, 41/41, 13 selectors, 6/6 executions with both EP13 stdout digests, and the 15/9/6 claim-binding sweep at zero mismatches. Nothing is edited, nothing is marked SATISFIED, condition 1 is not claimed discharged.

advisoriesList.observation: R6 states 'The blueprint table is a stale snapshot pending a blueprint successor' without naming who owns that successor or routing it to a specific later act.
advisoriesList.whyItIsNotABlockerAndNotPartOfTheGrade: Blueprint reading rule 1 requires a stop and a recorded design delta; it requires no routing, and the draft satisfies it. More to the point, DR-001's own source-pin cell names v1-authority-baseline.json, v1-status-evidence.json and the claim matrix -- it does not pin the blueprint -- so the §1.1 staleness sits outside DR-001's cited-property set under D-044 scope and cannot re-open this row or bear on its acceptance. I record this as explicitly outside the grade rather than letting it look like a condition on it.
advisoriesList.whyItIsWorthRecording: The corpus has a precedent form for exactly this residual: when I raised the unrouted claim-matrix pin as C2-D044-01, D-044 turn 2 named it, scoped it out, and routed it 'to a later file-09 D-000 act' -- and D-046 then performed that act. R6 names the delta and states the live binding, which is the hard part; adding 'routed to a later blueprint D-000 act' would close it the same way. Without a route the blueprint's CLAIMS row stays stale with no owner named.

whatIVerifiedByMeasurement: Subject digest at start and end: 5f97c7eeb55bcdcf2c237a6e3f0cadcd09927a1ec57186831b7927237bb782bf both times, matching the dispatch. No drift.

C2-SAT-B1 landed in full and in the form I specified. The lead now reads 'Both occurrences of "readiness condition 1 nets to zero `SATISFIED` rows until that re-record lands" and the clause "the row's LIVE standing is **OPEN**" cease to be live standing and remain history.' It names BOTH occurrences rather than one, which was the specific trap I flagged, and it disposes of the present-tense live-standing clause that was the more serious half.

The condition-1 accounting I asked for is present and correct: 'New condition-1 accounting: DR-001 becomes the first `SATISFIED` row of the eleven; condition 1 still does not discharge.' I verified the arithmetic against file 08 at turn 1 -- of DR-001..011, none is SATISFIED today and DR-008 is PARTIALLY SATISFIED, which is not SATISFIED -- so 'the first of the eleven' is accurate.

CX-DR001-D044-B1 is real and I verified it independently at the bytes rather than accepting the disposition table. Blueprint §1.1's CLAIMS row pins claim-register.v1.json at 95097b3fbb8986fc1761511059cfb8210dd2a2bc80b409f604fb1809405453d0. Live and baseline agree; the blueprint is the outlier. R6's digests are both quoted correctly.

R6's governing-rule citation is faithful, which I checked verbatim because the whole disposition rests on it. Blueprint §1.1 reading rule 1 reads: '**The digest is the contract.** Recompute `shasum -a 256` before porting any vector. If a file's digest differs from the value below, stop and record a design delta; do not build the bytes you found.' R6 applies exactly that: it stops, records the delta, names the live binding as authoritative, and states that this act does not edit the blueprint. The rule's operative consequence -- do not build the bytes you found -- constrains porting, not the register's accounting.

The attack 'CX-DR001-D044-B1 treated as no-conflict' fails. R6 names it a conflict, states both digests in full, identifies which side is live, and carries it in the 'Carry as named deltas, not silent conflicts' list rather than in a resolved column.

The blueprint is not among them, so under D-044's live scope -- the row re-opens only on a cited property-pin change -- a stale blueprint table neither re-opens DR-001 nor sits inside its acceptance surface.

reviewerSelfCorrection.what: I missed CX-DR001-D044-B1. requiredSelector #1 is 'IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md#section-1.1-pin-table'. At turn 1 I verified that the named section resolves -- the heading exists exactly once -- and recorded '13/13 resolve'. I never opened the pin table and compared its entries against live bytes, which is where the stale CLAIMS digest sits.
reviewerSelfCorrection.pattern: Verifying that a selector resolves without verifying what it resolves to. This is the third time I have recorded this family in this protocol: it produced my v1 section31 miss on the bound heads, it produced my too-narrow S31V3-01, and it produced this. The failure is the same each time -- I treat resolution as the check when resolution is only the precondition for the check.
reviewerSelfCorrection.whyItMattersMoreHere: This was the SATISFIED gate, the highest-stakes review in the corpus, and the missed item was a genuine stop-class name/digest conflict against a document the baseline's own authorityRule tells a reader to verify. My turn-1 verdict direction was right for a different reason, so the miss did not change the outcome, but that is luck rather than method.
reviewerSelfCorrection.correctionApplied: For a selector of the form 'document#section-table', resolution means enumerating the table's rows and comparing every pinned digest against live bytes -- not confirming the heading exists. I applied that this turn to reach the blueprint CLAIMS row myself and to re-derive both sides of R6's digest pair before accepting the disposition.

verdictNote: SATISFIED-GRADE. Both turn-1 blockers are repaired, and I graded each against the standard that governs it rather than against the disposition table. Mine was repaired in the exact form I specified, including naming both occurrences and adding the condition-1 accounting. The one I missed was repaired under blueprint reading rule 1, whose text I read verbatim before accepting that recording a design delta is the prescribed disposition rather than a way of proceeding past a stop. I re-ran every measurement this turn rather than relying on 'unchanged from turn 1', and all of it holds: 49/49, 41/41, 13 selectors, 6/6 executions with both EP13 stdout digests, 15 claim bindings at zero mismatches. My single advisory is expressly outside the grade -- DR-001 does not pin the blueprint, so the §1.1 staleness cannot re-open this row -- and asks only that the blueprint successor be routed the way D-044 routed the claim-matrix pin. On these measurements a file-08-only SATISFIED re-record is lawful. I record without qualification that I missed the blueprint conflict at turn 1 by checking that a selector resolved rather than what it resolved to, which is the third instance of that pattern I have had to correct in this protocol.
